summary: **Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member** **Power Grid Corporation of India Limited,** ‘SAUDAMINI’, Plot No-2, Sector-29, Gurgaon – 122 001 (Haryana). **.....Petitioner** |**Parties Present** **:** Shri Venkatesh, Advocate, PGCIL | |---| |Shri Ashutosh K. Shrivastava, Advocate, PGCIL| |Shri Akash Lamba, Advocate, PGCIL| |Shri Adarsh Singh, Advocate, PGCIL| |Shri Karan Arora, Advocate, PTCUL| |Shri Zafrul Hasan, PGCIL| |Shri Ranjeet Pandey, PGCIL | |Shri Vishal Sagar, PGCIL| |Shri Arjun Malhotra, PGCIL| |Shri Ashish Alankar, PGCIL| |Ms. Kirti, PGCIL| The instant Petition has been filed by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited, for determination of the tariff for the period from the COD to 31.3.2024 under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 (hereinafter referred to as “the 2019 Tariff Regulations”) in respect of the following assets (herein referred to as “the transmission assets”) under the “System Strengthening Scheme in Northern Region–XXXVII (NRSS-XXXVII)” (herein referred to as the “transmission project”): 2. The details of the transmission assets including scheduled commercial operation **_*_** _The Petitioner has claimed the COD of Asset-2 under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, since, the downstream asset under the scope of PTCUL is not ready._ **_**_** _The Petitioner has claimed the COD for Asset-3 under Regulations 76 and 77 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, i.e., under “Power to relax” and “Power to Remove Difficulty”, vide affidavit dated 29.8.2024._ 3. The Petitioner has claimed the COD of Asset-2 as 5.1.2023 under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, since the associated downstream line for Asset-2 under the scope of PTCUL is not ready. 5. The Petitioner has further submitted that this issue was discussed in the 49 th TCC & 72 nd NRPC held on 29-30 March 2024, and the following was agreed: Main Bay 203 at Jauljivi Sub-station”. Accordingly, the Petitioner has claimed COD of Asset-3 under Regulations 76 and 77 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, i.e., “Power to Relax” and “Power to remove Difficulty” considering the capitalisation of it, being agreed in the NRPC. 7. The Petition was heard on 20.11.2025. During the course of the hearing, the representative of the Petitioner prayed for an interim tariff for the transmission assets. 8. The Respondent has submitted a reply vide affidavit dated 9.2.2024, and accordingly, the Petitioner has filed a rejoinder vide affidavit dated 16.5.2024. However, the submissions will be analysed during the preparation of the final tariff order. 9. We have considered the submissions and prayers of the Petitioner for the interim _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these regulations and is adequate for carrying out prudence check of the claims made, the Commission may consider granting interim tariff in case of new projects._ _(6) The Commission may hear the petitioner, the respondents and any other person permitted including the consumers or consumer associations while granting interim or final tariff._ _(7) The difference between the tariff determined in accordance with clauses (3) and (5) above and clauses (4) and (5) above, shall be recovered from or refunded to, the beneficiaries or the long term customers, as the case may be, with simple interest at the rate equal to the bank rate prevailing as on 1st April of the respective year of the tariff period, in six equal monthly instalments._ 11. After carrying out a preliminary prudence check and going through the documents placed on records, it has been observed that the Petitioner has submitted that the RLDC trial run for Asset-1 was completed from 20.11.2022 to 3.12.2022, and the COD for Asset-1 has been claimed w.e.f. 4.12.2022 with a time overrun of 1612 days. Therefore, taking into consideration the AFC claimed by the Petitioner and the time over-run in case of Asset-1, we hereby, allow the interim tariff @ 70% of the claimed AFC in respect of Asset-1 for the FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24 in terms of Regulation 10(3) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations subject to the final tariff order for Asset1 after the detailed analysis. 12. The Petitioner has further claimed the COD of Asset-2 under Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. Regulation 5(2) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations provides as under: _“In case the transmission system or element thereof executed by a transmission licensee is ready for commercial operation but the interconnected generating station or the transmission system of other transmission licensee as per the agreed project implementation schedule is not ready for commercial operation, the transmission licensee may file petition before the Commission for approval of the date of commercial operation of such transmission system or element thereof.”_ 14. The Petitioner has also claimed the COD of the Asset-3 under Regulations 76 and 77 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, i.e., under “Power to Relax” and “Power to Remove Difficulty”, respectively, and the same shall be dealt with in the final tariff order. 15. Thus, the annual transmission charges claimed by the Petitioner for Asset-1 are as under: 17. The interim tariff allowed in this order will be applicable from the COD of Asset1, and the billing, collection, and disbursement of the transmission charges approved in this order shall be governed by the provisions of the 2020 Sharing Regulations as provided in Regulation 57 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, as amended from time to time. 18. Further, the interim transmission charges allowed in this order shall be subject to adjustment as per Regulation 10 of the 2019 Tariff Regulations.
